slides.texte_overlay:
winter habits that keep
your mood from sinking

morning light

get outside within an hour of waking, even when it's grey. morning daylight sets your body clock and lifts your mood more than you'd expect. it sounds simple, but very few people actually do it.

moving every day

take a brisk walk or do ten minutes of stretching daily. movement warms you up and releases the feel good chemicals that winter quietly steals. over time, it quietly changes how you feel every day.

cosy evening rituals

make your evenings something to look forward to: warm tea, soft light, a good book. small comforts make the dark months feel gentle instead of heavy. it honestly works.

learning by the fire

dark evenings are perfect for learning something beautiful, a constellation, a myth or a painting. it's a small change with a surprisingly big effect.

learning by the fire

dark evenings are perfect for curiosity. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson a day, a myth or a constellation, and 5 minutes makes winter nights feel cosy.

slides.texte_overlay:
seeing people

plan one meet up a week, even a short coffee. winter makes it easy to hide away, but real connection is one of the best protections for your mood. try it for one week and notice the difference.
